principles: Evidence, not human blame, decides advisory activation.
Activation must be usable via explicit CLI apply when evidence and reviewed policy are present, not permanently default-off.
Learning remains non-authoritative and never becomes gate evidence.
Every activation must be digest-bound, idempotent, auditable, and reversible.
Do not optimize arbitrarily; only close the real correctness gap between recommendation and runtime consumption.
drivers: Hundreds of historical experiences make per-candidate manual activation unscalable.
Bad automatic activation can mislead future agents, so evidence thresholds and rollback are mandatory.
Existing B-9958 V1 artifacts should be reused instead of inventing a new learning store.

options.name: manual-activation-only
cons: Does not solve the user problem
Does not scale to hundreds of experiences

options.name: evidence-activated-apply
pros: Keeps activation explicit, auditable, digest-bound, and reversible
cons: Requires careful test fixtures and policy checks

rationale: Choose a real evidence-activated apply path: the CLI should activate eligible advisory playbooks when the policy and evidence pass, while blocking weak or stale candidates with precise reasons.

preMortem.scenario: Weak candidate is activated because neutral observations are counted as evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Aggregation denominator includes neutral or unknown outcomes.
preMortem.consequence: Runtime guidance becomes noisy and agents may repeat bad advice.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep decisiveSamples equal helped + dismissed + harmful and add tests proving neutral/unknown/DONE settlement cannot activate.

preMortem.scenario: Stale or duplicated candidate is activated.
preMortem.trigger: Apply ignores candidate digest or source-lineage duplicate blockers.
preMortem.consequence: Wrong playbook becomes active or duplicate lessons pollute runtime memory.
preMortem.mitigation: Require current digest, clean lineage, and idempotency keys; add stale/duplicate negative tests.

preMortem.scenario: Auto activation becomes another default-off fake feature.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation keeps requiring an unset environment flag or throws after guards pass.
preMortem.consequence: User still cannot use the activation path and V1 remains incomplete.
preMortem.mitigation: Make reviewed policy plus qualifying evidence sufficient for explicit --apply in local CLI tests; remove the always-off activationImplemented=false blocker.

preMortem.trigger: Demotion deletes rows or overwrites original activation/outcome history.
preMortem.consequence: Auditing cannot explain why a playbook was active or removed.
preMortem.mitigation: Use append-only audit/provenance and status transitions; never delete playbook/outcome/decision rows.
